9642.d: 1. to be fond of strife, engage in eager rivalry, be contentious , φιλονεικῶν out of contentiousness or party spirit , (Thucydides); φ. πρός τινα (Lysias Orator):—;with accusative, φ. τὸ ἐμὲ εἶναι τὸν ἀποκρινόμενον to be eager that I should be the answerer, (Plato Philosophus); τὰ χείρω φ. to be so obstinate as to choose the worst, (Thucydides) • 2. in good sense, to struggle emulously , φ. περὶ τῶν καλλίστων (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

9643.d: 1. a muzzle , Lat. capistrum, (Lucian) • 2. the nose-band of a horse's bridle, fitted with pipes through which the horses' breath made a whistling sound, (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 3. a kind of cup , used as a dice-box , Lat. fritillus, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

9644.d: to be heated, inflamed, to fester , φλεγμαίνουσα πόλις, opposite to ὑγιής, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

9645.d: 1. transitive to burn, burn up , (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass. to take fire, blaze up , (Iliad by Homer) • 2. metaphorically to kindle, inflame with passion, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., like Lat. uri, to burn with passion, be inflamed, (Sophocles Tragicus) • 3. to light up , Ζεὺς βέλος φλέγων making it blaze or flash , (Aeschulus Tragicus); metaphorically, ἄταν οὐρανίαν φλέγων letting the flame of mischief blaze up to heaven, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to blaze up, be a-light , (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 4. metaphorically to make illustrious or famous , Lat. illustrare, (Pindar):—;Pass. to be or become so , (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 5. intransitive to burn, flame, blaze ,…

9646.d: 1. a vein , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; φλέβα σχάζειν to open a vein , (Xenophon Historicus) • 2. a vein of metal, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

9647.d: in plural φλιαί, = σταθμοί, the doorposts, jambs , (Odyssey by Homer); in singular, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

9653.d: purple-red, purple or crimson , and (generally) red , Lat. puniceus, (Herdotus Historicus):—;attic contracted φοινι-κοῦς, ᾶ, οῦν, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

9662.d: 1. a shuddering, shivering , (Plato Philosophus) • 2. shuddering , especially from religious awe, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

9664.d: that causes shuddering, horrible , (Euripides):—;neuter φρικῶδες, as adverb horribly , (Euripides):—; adverb -δῶς, Sup., φρικωδέστατα ἔχειν to be in utter horror , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

9665.d: 1. thought, care, heed, attention bestowed upon a person or thing, with genitive, φροντίδ᾽ ἔχειν τινός (Euripides); ἐν φροντίδι εἶναι περί τινος (Herdotus Historicus) • 2. absolute thought, meditation , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐν φροντίδι μοι ἐγένετο [ τὸ πρῆγμα] (Herdotus Historicus); ἐμβῆσαί τινα ἐς φροντίδα to set one a thinking , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;in plural thoughts , αἱ δεύτεραί πως φροντίδες σοφώτεραι (Euripides) • 3. deep thought, care, concern , (Aeschulus Tragicus); οὐ φροντὶς Ἱπποκλείδῃ no matter to Hippocleides! (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

9666.d: 1. a looking out, watch, guard , as a duty, (Herdotus Historicus); φρουρὰν ἄζηλον ὀχήσω shall keep unenviable watch , (Aeschulus Tragicus); φρουρὰ ὄμματος my watchful eye, (Sophocles Tragicus); φρουρᾶς ᾄδειν to sing while on guard , (Aristophanes Comicus) • 2. a prison , (Plato Philosophus) • 3. of persons, a watch, guard, garrison , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; especially of frontier-posts , which were guarded in Attica by the περίπολοι, (Xenophon Historicus) • 4. at Sparta, a body of men destined for service , φρουρὰν φαίνειν (see. φαίνω A. 1. 5). (ML)

9668.d: 1. a violent snorting, neighing , (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 2. metaphorically wanton behaviour, insolence , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

9670.d: 1. to roast or fry , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρετμοῖσι φρύξουσι they shall cook with the [wood of] the oars, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., πεφρυγμέναι κριθαί roasted barley, (Thucydides) • 2. of the sun, to parch , Lat. torrere, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

9674.d: to drive from a country, banish , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

9675.d: 1. one who flees from his country, a runaway, fugitive, a banished man, exile, refugee , Lat. exul, profugus, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; φυγάδα ποιεῖν τινα (Xenophon Historicus); κατάγειν φυγάδας to recall them; etc. • 2. of an army, put to flight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

9676.d: 1. growth, stature , especially fine growth, noble stature , (Homer); Νέστορι εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε φυήν τt ἄγχιστα ἐῴκει he was like Nestor both in shape and size and stature (or growth) , (Iliad by Homer) • 2. poetry for φύσις, one's natural powers, nature, genius , (Pindar) • 3. the flower or prime of age , (Pindar) (ML)

9679.d: 1. the chief of a φυ_λή, a phylarch , (Herdotus Historicus):—;used to translated the Rom. tribunus , (Plutarch) • 2. at Athens, the commander of the cavalry furnished by each tribe , see. ἵππαρχος. (ML)

9681.d: 1. to mix flour or meal so as to make it into dough, to knead , (Herdotus Historicus); γῆν φυράσειν φόνῳ to make earth into a bloody paste , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., οἴνῳ καὶ ἐλαίῳ πεφυραμένα ἄλφιτα (Thucydides) • 2. metaphorically, μαλακὴν φωνὴν φυράσασθαι to make up a soft voice, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

9683.d: 1. to mix something dry with something wet , mostly with a sense of mixing so as to soil or defile , δάκρυσιν εἵματ᾽ ἔφυρον they wetted, sullied their garments with tears, (Iliad by Homer); also with genitive, χείλεα φύρσω αἵματος (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., δάκρυσι πεφυρμένη (Iliad by Homer); αἵματι οἶκος ἐφύρθη (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 2. of dry things, κόνει φύρουσα κάρα (Euripides); γαίαι πεφύρσεσθαι κόμαν to be doomed to have one's hair defiled with earth, (Pindar) • 3. metaphorically to mingle together, confuse , ἔφυρον εἰκῆ πάντα they mixed all things up together, did all at random, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be mixed up , ἐκ πεφυρμένου καὶ θηριώδους…

9684.d: 1. transitive to puff or blow up, distend , (Aristophanes Comicus); of bag-pipers, (Aristophanes Comicus); φ. τὰς γνάθους to puff them out , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be inflated , ἡ γαστὴρ ἐπεφύσητό μοι (Aristophanes Comicus) • 2. metaphorically to puff one up, make him vain , and so to cheat , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be puffed up , ἐπί τινι at a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) • 3. to blow up, kindle a fire: but also • 4. to blow out, extinguish , τὴν λαμπάδα (Aristophanes Comicus) • 5. to blow out, spurt out , (Sophocles Tragicus) • 6. to blow a wind-instrument, (Euripides) (ML)

9685.d: an instrument for blowing, blowpipe or tube , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

9687.d: 1. that which has grown, a plant, tree , (Iliad by Homer), etc. • 2. generally a creature , of men, (Euripides) • 3. like ἔρνος, of men, a descendant, child , (Euripides) (ML)

9688.d: 1. to search after a thief or theft, search a house , (Aristophanes Comicus) • 2. in Pass. to be detected , (Demosthenes Orator); with participle, κλέπτης ὢν φωρᾶσθαι (Demosthenes Orator); so, κακὸς [ ὢν] ἐφωράθη φίλοις (Euripides):—;also of things, ἀργύριον ἐφωράθη ἐξαγόμενον money was discovered to be in course of exportation, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

9693.d: 1. a small stone, pebble , in plural, (Lucian), etc. • 2. as collect. in singular, gravel, rubble , used in building, (Thucydides); so also in plural, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

9694.d: 1. a smith's shop, forge, smithy , (Herdotus Historicus) • 2. = χαλκίον, a copper, caldron , (Herdotus Historicus) • 3. a metal reflector in a lamp, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

9695.d: of copper or bronze, brasen , (Homer); χαλκήιος δόμος, = χαλκεῖον, a forge , (Odyssey by Homer); χάλκειον γένος, of the Age of brass , (Hesiod) (ML)

9696.d: 1. to make of copper or (generally) of metal, to forge , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;Mid. to forge for oneself , (Theognis Elegiacus):—;Pass. to be wrought or forged , (Aristophanes Comicus) • 2. absolute to be a smith, work as a smith, ply the hammer , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ χαλκεύειν the smith's art , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

9697.d: the chameleon , a kind of lizard known for changing its colour, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

9698.d: 1. chaos , the first stateof the universe, (Hesiod), etc. • 2. infinite space, the expanse , (Aristophanes Comicus) • 3. the nether abyss, infinite darkness , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

9699.d: perhaps a yellowish bird dwelling in clefts the curlew , (Aristophanes Comicus): χαραδριοῦ βίον ζῆν, of a glutton, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

9701.d: to fence by a palisade, fortify , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

9703.d: 1. to make sharp or pointed, sharpen, whet , (Hesiod) • 2. to furnish with notches or teeth , like a saw, (Aristotle Philosopher):—;Pass., σκύταλον κεχ. ὄζοις a staff jagged or rugged with branches, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): metaphorically, [ ὄμμα] ἠλεμάτοις ἀκτῖσι χαράσσεται sparkles with false lights, of the effect produced by painting the eye-lids, [variant datesAnthology Palantina • 3. metaphorically in Pass., κεχαραγμένος τινί exasperated at any one, (Herdotus Historicus); κείνῳ τόδε μὴ χαράσσου be not angry at him for this, (Euripides) • 4. to cut into furrows, cut, scratch , (Pindar):—;Pass., κέκοπται καὶ χαράσσεται πέδον (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 5. to…

9704.d: 1. a joy , (Euripides); plural joys, delights , (Euripides) • 2. = χάρμα II, joy, delight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

9710.d: 1. of or in winter, of or in winter-time , opposite to θερινός, χ. τροπαί (see. τροπή 1), (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὴν χ. (i.e. ὥρην); during the winter season , (Herdotus Historicus) • 2. wintry , (Thucydides); see. χειμέριος. (ML)

9712.d: 1. a voting or electing by show of hands , (Thucydides) • 2. a vote , Lat. suffragium, in plural, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

9713.d: 1. to bring into hand, to manage, master, subdue , (Aristophanes Comicus) • 2. mostly in Mid., to conquer, overpower, subdue , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τήνδ᾽ ἐχειρούμην ἄγραν became master of this booty, (Sophocles Tragicus) • 3. without any sense of violence, to master, subdue , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. • 4. χειροῦμαι is also Pass. to be subdued , [variant datesTragica Adespota; future χειρωθήσομαι (Demosthenes Orator); aor1 ἐχειρώθην (Herdotus Historicus); perfect κεχείρωμαι (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

9714.d: 1. the swallow , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; the twittering of the swallow was proverbially used of barbarous tongues by the Greeks, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χελιδόνων μουσεῖα (see. μουσεῖον); proverbs also, μία χελιδὼν ἔαρ οὐ ποιεῖ (Aristotle Philosopher) • 2. the frog in a horse's foot , so called from its being forked like the swallow's tail , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

9715.d: 1. a tortoise , (Homeric Hymns); prov. of insensibility, ἰὼ χελῶναι μακάριαι τοῦ δέρματος oh ye tortoises , happy in your thick skins! (Aristophanes Comicus) • 2. like Roman testudo, a pent-house formed of shields overlapping each other like the scales on a tortoise's back , used by storming parties in approaching a city's walls: then, generally, a pent-house for protecting besiegers, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

9718.d: on or of dry land , ὄρνιθες χ. land- birds, opposite to λιμναῖοι, (Herdotus Historicus); χ. κροκόδειλος a lizard, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also of landsmen , as opposite to seamen, (Euripides); κῦμα χερσαῖον στρατοῦ, an army, opposite to a fleet, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

9719.d: 1. dry land, land , ἐπὶ χέρσου, opposite to ἐν πόντῳ, (Odyssey by Homer); κύματα κυλινδόμενα προτὶ χέρσον (Odyssey by Homer); κῦμα χέρσῳ ῥηγνύμενον (Iliad by Homer); χέρσῳ on or by land , (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 2. as adjective, χέρσος, ον, dry, firm , of land, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν κονίᾳ χέρσῳ, opposite to πόντῳ, (Pindar) • 3. dry, hard, barren , (Herdotus Historicus); χ. λιμήν a harbour left dry , [variant datesAnthology Palantina • 4. metaphorically barren, without children , of women, (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive barren of , πυρὰ χέρσος ἀγλαϊσμάτων (Euripides) • Prob. from same Root as ξηρός. (ML)

9721.d: 1. Radic. sense, to pour : • 2. properly of liquids, to pour out, pour , (Homer), etc.; Zeus χέει ὕδωρ, i. e. he makes it rain, (Iliad by Homer); χέει χιόνα βορέας (Euripides); absolute, χέει it snows , (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid. to pour for oneself , especially of drink-offerings, χοὰς χεόμην νεκύεσσι (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Pass., χέονται κρῆναι they gush forth , (Euripides); χυθέντος ποτοῦ ἐς γῆν (Sophocles Tragicus) • 3. χ. δάκρυα to shed tears, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., of tears, to pour or gush forth , (Homer); so of blood, to be shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 4. in Pass. to become liquid, melt, thaw , (Xenophon Historicus) • 5. of solids, to shed, scatter ,…

9722.d: 1. a horse's hoof , (Hesiod):—;also, a cloven hoof , (Euripides) • 2. in plural, of the talons of a bird, [variant datesTragica Adespota; of a wolf's claws , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) • 3. a sea-bank, breakwater , formed of stones laid at the base of a sea-wall, to break the force of the waves (so called because it projected like a hoof) , Lat. crepido, (Thucydides) • 4. the spur of a mountain or ridge of rocks answering a like purpose, (Thucydides) • 5. a cloven implement , such as a netting-needle;—; compare χηλεύω. (ML)

9725.d: 1. intransitive to be bereaved of a person or thing, with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) • 2. absolute to be bereaved of a husband, to be widowed, live in widowhood , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.;—;of a man, to be a widower , (Plutarch); so, χηρεύσει λέχος (Euripides) • 3. to live in solitude , of an exile, (Sophocles Tragicus) • 4. transitive to bereave , (Euripides) (ML)

9726.d: of yesterday , τὸ χθιζὸν χρεῖος their yesterday's debt, (Iliad by Homer); ὁ χθ. πόνος yesterday's labour, (Herdotus Historicus); in adverbial sense, with Verbs, χθιζὸς ἔβη he went yesterday , (Iliad by Homer); χθ. ἤλυθες (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;neuter χθιζόν as adverb = χθές, (Homer); so plural χθιζά, see. πρώιζος. (ML)

9727.d: 1. the earth, ground , (Homer); χθόνα δῦναι to go beneath the earth , i. e. to die, (Iliad by Homer); κατὰ χθονὸς κρύπτειν τινά (Sophocles Tragicus); κούφα σοι χθὼν ἐπάνω πέσοι (Euripides) • 2. of the nether world , οἱ ὑπὸ χθονός, i. e. those in the shades below , Lat. inferi, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κατὰ χθονὸς θεαί, i. e. the Erinyes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 3. earth , i. e. the whole earth, the world , (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 4. Earth , as a goddess, (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 5. a particular land or country , of Ithaca, (Odyssey by Homer); of Libya, (Pindar); χθὼν Ἀσιᾶτις, Δωρίς, Ἀργεία, Ἑλλάς, Ἰδαία, etc., [variant datesTragica Adespota (ML)

9728.d: unripe wheaten groats , as ἄλφιτα are barley-groats, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

9729.d: 1. the office or post of χιλίαρχος, (Xenophon Historicus) • 2. the office of the tribuni militares , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

9732.d: 1. a she-goat , Lat. capra, (Iliad by Homer), attic • 2. Χίμαιρα, ἡ, Chimaera , a firespouting-monster, with lion's head, serpent's tail, and goat's body, killed by Bellerophon, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

9733.d: 1. a he-goat , Lat. caper, = τράγος, (Aristophanes Comicus) • 2. also feminine = χίμαιρα, [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

9735.d: Lat. laena, a large square upper-garment, a cloak, mantle, (Homer); it was made of wool, and worn over the χιτών, thrown over the shoulders, fastened with a pin or brooch περόνη). It is also called φᾶρος by (Homer), and in later Greek ἱμάτιον, Latin pallium. • derivation uncertain (ML)

9741.d: 1. any light porous substance , ἁλὸς χνόος the foam that gathers at the edge of the sea, (Odyssey by Homer); πωλικὸς χν. horse's foam , [variant datesAnthology Palantina • 2. the first down on the chin of youths, Lat. lanugo, (Aristophanes Comicus): the bloom on fruit, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

9744.d: 1. like χόλη, gall, bile , (Iliad by Homer) • 2. generally metaphorically bile, gall, bitter anger, wrath , (Homer), attic; χόλος ἔδυ τινά (Iliad by Homer); χόλος ἔμπεσε θυμῷ (Iliad by Homer); χόλον πέσσειν, καταπέσσειν (see. entry); χ. σβέσσαι παῦσαι (Iliad by Homer); χόλου παύεσθαι (Hesiod):—;with genitive objecti, anger towards or because of another, (Iliad by Homer); with genitive rei, anger for, because of a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus) • 3. an object of anger , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

9746.d: 1. gut-string, the string of a lyre, Lat. chorda, (Odyssey by Homer) • 2. tripe , (Batrachomyomachia): also = χόρδευμα, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

9747.d: 1. to dance a round or choral dance , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; especially of the Bacchic chorus, (Euripides):—; to take part in the chorus , regarded as a matter of religion, (Sophocles Tragicus): to be one of a chorus , (Aristophanes Comicus): —;with dative pers. to dance to him, in his honour , (Euripides) • 2. generally, to dance , especially from joy, (Sophocles Tragicus) • 3. metaphorically to practise a thing, be versed in it, (Plato Philosophus) • 4. with accusative cognate, φροίμιον χορεύσομαι I will dance a prelude (to festivities), (Aeschulus Tragicus); χ. γάμους to celebrate them, (Euripides); ὄργια Μουσῶν (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Mid., χορεύεσθαι δίνας…

9748.d: 1. the office of a χορηγός at Athens, the defraying of the cost of the public choruses , being the chief of the λειτουργίαι, (Thucydides), etc. • 2. means for providing χοροί: abundance of means, fortune , (Aristotle Philosopher) • 3. metaphorically supplies for war , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

9749.d: the membrane that encloses the fetus, the afterbirth , Lat. secundae: plural χόρια, ων, τά, a dish made by stuffing it with honey and milk , a kind of haggis , (Aristophanes Comicus): proverbial, χαλεπὸν χορίω (doric genitive) κύνα γεῦσαι "don't let a dog taste blood, " (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (cf. Horace, canis a corio nunquam absterrebitur uncto). (ML)

9751.d: a being fed, feasting , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

9753.d: a coos, a measurement of liquid (Lev.19.36)

9754.d: to neigh, whinny , Lat. hinnire, of horses, (Iliad by Homer), etc. • Formed from the sound. (ML)

9756.d: 1. that which one needs must pay, an obligation, debt , (Odyssey by Homer); a debt for stolen cattle , (Iliad by Homer); χρεῖος ἀποστήσασθαι to pay a debt in full, (Iliad by Homer); ἀρᾶς τίνει χρ. pays the debt demanded by the curse, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χρέος πόλει προσάπτειν to attach a further debt , i.e. guilt to the city, (Sophocles Tragicus); χρέος ἀποδιδόναι to repay a debt , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural debts , χρειῶν λύσις (Hesiod); τὴν οὐσίαν ἅπασαν χρέα κατέλιπε left all the property in outstanding debts , (Demosthenes Orator) • 2. a needful business, an affair, matter , ἑὸν αὐτοῦ χρεῖος (Odyssey by Homer): a requirement, a purpose , (Sophocles…

9757.d: to utter oracles, divine , (Aristophanes Comicus) • from χρησμολόγος (ML)

9759.d: 1. the surface of a body, the skin; the body itself, (Iliad by Homer) • 2. the superficial appearance of a thing, its colour , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;especially the colour of the skin, the complexion , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

9762.d: 1. one who melts gold , of one who gilds the horns of a victim, (Odyssey by Homer) • 2. a goldsmith , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

9765.d: 1. poured, shed , αἷμα χυτόν blood shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) • 2. of dry things, shot out, heaped up , χυτὴ γαῖα a mound of earth, a sepulchral mound, (Homer):—;as Substantive, χυτός, οῦ, = χῶμα, a mound, bank, dike , (Herdotus Historicus) • 3. melted , ἀρτήματα λίθινα χυτά pendants of melted stone, (Herdotus Historicus) • 4. generally, liquid, flowing , [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

9766.d: 1. an earthen pot, a pot for boiling, pipkin , Lat. olla, (Aristophanes Comicus) • 2. χύτραι, pots of pulse offered to inferior deities, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

9768.d: a pot with feet , or a portable stove for putting a pot upon, (Hesiod) (ML)

9770.d: to be or go lame , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

9771.d: 1. earth thrown up, a bank, mound , thrown up against the walls of cities to take them, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a dike to hinder a river from overflowing, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a dam , (Herdotus Historicus):—; a mole or pier , carried out into the sea, Lat. moles, (Herdotus Historicus) • 2. like Lat. tumulus, a sepulchral mound, [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesTragica Adespota • (ML)

9779.d: 1. to cast into a mould ( χόανος), (Aristophanes Comicus) • 2. to cast metal: —;Pass., κεχωνευμένος (Plutarch) (ML)

9782.d: 1. a pair of scissors , Lat. forfex, [variant datesAnthology Palantina • 2. a building with a pointed stone roof, a vault , Lat. fornix, (Sophocles Tragicus) • Deriv. unknown. (ML)
